data.name: Meshach
data.gender_notes: Meshach is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Meshach means 'God's gift' in Hebrew. This name is biblically significant in the Old Testament as the name of one of the three Hebrew men who refused to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image. The name Meshach carries the meaning “God's gift” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Meshach usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's blessings and divine intervention.
data.etymology: Meshach belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Meshach total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: משך
in_hebrew.meaning: משך הוא מי שמשך או מושך את האנשים אל האל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: משך הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'מי שמשך או מושך את האנשים אל האל'. השם משך מוזכר בספר דניאל, פרק 1, פסוק 6, כאחד משלושת החברים של המלך נבוכדנצר, ששימשו כמשרתים גבוהים בממלכתו. השם משך נגזר מהשורש 'משך', שפירושו 'למשוך' או 'להוביל'. השם משך הוא גם קיצור של השם 'משכאל', שפירושו 'מי שמשך את האל'. השם משך הוא שם נפוץ בקרב היהודים והנוצרים כאחד.

in_greek.name: Μησάχ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Μησάχ είναι αυτός που τραβά ή οδηγεί τους ανθρώπους στον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Μησάχ είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα 'משך' (Meshach). Το όνομα Μησάχ αναφέρεται στο βιβλίο του Δανιήλ, κεφάλαιο 1, στίχος 6, ως ένα από τους τρεις φίλους του βασιλιά Ναβουχοδονόσορ, που υπηρετούσαν ως υψηλοί αξιωματούχοι στο βασίλειό του. Το όνομα Μησάχ προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό ρίζα 'משך' (mashakh), που σημαίνει 'να τραβά' ή 'να οδηγεί'. Το όνομα Μησάχ είναι επίσης συντομογραφία του ονόματος 'משכאל' (Meshkhael), που σημαίνει 'αυτός που τραβά τον Θεό'.

in_latin.name: Meshach
in_latin.meaning: Meshach is one who draws or leads people to God
in_latin.long_meaning: Meshach is a Latinized form of the Hebrew name 'משך' (Meshach). The name Meshach is mentioned in the book of Daniel, chapter 1, verse 6, as one of the three friends of King Nebuchadnezzar, who served as high officials in his kingdom. The name Meshach is derived from the Hebrew root 'משך' (mashakh), which means 'to draw' or 'to lead'. The name Meshach is also a shortened form of the name 'משכאל' (Meshkhael), which means 'one who draws God'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Meshach is of Hebrew origin and has strong cultural connections to the ancient Israelites. In the Old Testament book of Daniel, Meshach is one of the three Hebrew men, along with Shadrach and Abednego, who refused to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image. Their unwavering faith and bravery in the face of persecution is a powerful reminder of the Israelites' unwavering commitment to their God.
data.spiritual_significance: Meshach is a name that carries deep spiritual significance as it means 'God's gift.' It is a reminder that every individual is a unique creation of God, given as a gift to the world. It also serves as a reminder that each person has the potential to make a meaningful impact on the world, just as Meshach and his companions did when they stood up for their faith. Ultimately, the name Meshach encourages us to recognize and celebrate the divine nature of ourselves and others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Meshach in Hebrew means "Who is like God?" This name was given to one of the three Hebrew heroes in the Book of Daniel, who with his brothers Shadrach and Abednego, refused to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and were subsequently thrown into a burning fiery furnace. Meshach, along with his companions, remained unharmed, demonstrating the power and presence of God in their lives.
